newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds flat to softer ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds flat to softer ahead of FOMC.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds marked time on Monday as the near-term direction of short-term interest rates held in the balance and junk bond prices were flat to marginally lower, dealers across both markets said.

Investment grade spreads were mostly flat to softer in light activity, traders said, adding that trading in last week's large new issues generated the bulk of the action. The $4.3 billion Norfolk Southern deal, which tightened significantly when freed, was unchanged to slightly wider compared with best markets seen on Friday.
"Ahead of the Fed move the market has remained, and will remain, pretty quiet," one trader said. "Issuers have held off on talk and that ties the hands of a lot of people."

Chase Manhattan Corp's $300 million 10-year subordinated note issue of Friday, which priced at an aggressive 62 basis point spread, succumbed to the market's malaise and widened to a 64 bid on Monday, traders said. But the price action was not unusual given the uncertainty surrounding Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, they stressed.

In a Reuters survey of the 39 U.S. primary dealers, 21 expected the Fed to leave short-term rates unchanged, while the remaining 18 forecasting a 25 basis point hike in the 5.50 percent federal funds rate.

Turning to the high-yield market, the flurry of new issue trading gave way to a lackluster session on Monday and prices were flat to lower. Bids for zero coupon debt that had recenlty outperformed, such as U.K. cable companies and competitive local exchange carriers, fell by as much as one point, said buyside sources and traders.

Reflecting the moves, Diamond Cable Communications' zero coupon debt was bid at 60-1/4 on Monday compared with a market as high as 61-1/2 on Friday. McLeod zeros were also about one point lower at 60 bid, the manager said.
Still, volume on the day was extremely thin and actual levels were therefore difficult to prove. Cash paying high-yield issues were flat by all accounts.

Market participants also noted heady trade seen in the new issue market in the past few weeks may have run its course for the time being. The reason, one manager said, is pricings have rapidly returned to the aggressive levels seen in February.
Some issues of late last week, including Pogo Producing Co's 10-year debt, were seen flat to up 1/8 point when freed to trade compared with one to two point gains in many previous issues.
Also, Coleman zero coupon debt traded below its issued price of 64.949, one money manager said.

High-yield issues are accumulating rapidly, meanwhile, with about $1.0 billion set to price this week. Issues include Stone Container Corp's $250 million in five-year senior subordinated debt with supplemental interest certificates; Chief Auto Parts Inc's $125 million eight-year senior notes, and CLISA's $100 million seven-year guaranteed notes.

In the Treasury market, prices posted slight losses in a dull session as traders there kept to the sidelines ahead of FOMC. The benchmark 30-year bond was trading down 5/32 at 96-10/32 to yield 6.92 percent late in the session.
